transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Solutions), Sana (Aquila Head of AI), Tom (Platform), Lena (Product), Rajesh (Security)

Summary (auto): Discussed POC scope focusing on workload characterization — QPS, concurrency, token sizes, and benchmarks. Agreement to run a two-week POC with specific success criteria around latency, cost, and accuracy/regression thresholds.

[00:00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:00:04] Sana: yes, loud and clear, thanks Maya
[00:00:08] Maya: cool so the goals for today are pretty straightforward, we want to nail down the workload profile for the POC, agree success criteria and timeline, and make sure security and infra prerequisites are captured
[00:00:20] Tom: sounds good, high level we want to validate that Redwood can handle our peak qps and not blow up the cost, so tying both latency and cost is key
[00:00:30] Diego: great. quick intro from my side, i'll own the benchmark harness. i'll propose traffic patterns and we'll instrument latency P95/P99 and tokens per request
[00:00:40] Lena: and i'll be the product lead; success criteria for us is conversational correctness above our baseline and <150ms p95 for short queries if possible
[00:00:48] Maya: noted. can you share current numbers? what's your typical qps and payload distribution?
[00:00:56] Sana: yeah so production today averages around 12 qps globally for our conversational assistant, peaks around 60 qps during batch windows. for the POC we want to test up to 150 qps to understand headroom. tokens: 70% of requests are short (input 5-40 tokens, output 10-60 tokens), 25% medium (input 40-200, out 60-300), 5% long (input 200-1000, out 300-2000)
[00:01:25] Diego: ok that's useful. when you say peaks around 60, is that concurrent open sessions or requests per second?
[00:01:31] Sana: requests per second. concurrent sessions vary but usually ~40 concurrent websockets.
[00:01:36] Rajesh: security wise we need VPC peering or private link, and KMS integration for any keys. SOC2 is a must, and audit logs forwarded to our splunk instance
[00:01:47] Maya: totally reasonable. Redwood supports VPC private control plane and we can do customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. we'll attach SOC2 cert and the security questionnaire as part of the POC pack
[00:01:58] Tom: for benchmarks, are you suggesting we run hosted first and then dedicated? or go straight to dedicated?
[00:02:05] Diego: recommended path is: hosted baseline to get functional parity and initial latency/cost numbers, then dedicated reserved capacity for spike testing and predictability. quantization differences can change throughput as well, so we want to compare same model family on both configs
[00:02:20] Maya: and we have model variants — lite/quantized vs full fp16 — we'll document expected perf tradeoffs in the plan
[00:02:27] Lena: about success criteria, in addition to latency we need cost per 1M tokens target and regression threshold on hallucination/accuracy compared to our current model
[00:02:36] Sana: yes, our baseline is 92% intent accuracy on our eval set, we want no more than 2% regression and preferable parity
[00:02:44] Diego: will capture that. can you share eval sets and a small holdout? even ~1k queries helps for initial regressions
[00:02:50] Sana: will do.
[00:02:52] Maya: timeline wise what are you thinking?
[00:02:55] Tom: we want a two-week POC with the main benchmark run in week 2. goal to decide on Dedicated purchase by end of month if things look good
[00:03:04] Maya: ok so tentatively baseline hosted run week 1, dedicated spike tests week 2 (Aug 17-21 window). Diego, you ok to build traffic scripts covering 50/100/150 qps profiles?
[00:03:14] Diego: yep i'll prepare scripts and an orchestration plan. instrumenting P50/P95/P99 and token counts per second. also we'll produce cost-per-1M-token estimate per config
[00:03:25] Rajesh: on the network side we need to confirm allowed CIDR ranges and any egress rules. prefer private link over public endpoints if possible
[00:03:33] Maya: noted, we'll include a network checklist and a sample VPC peering flow in the POC doc.
[00:03:39] Lena: i have a quick question on caching; you mentioned KV cache in docs — how does that interact with concurrency and stateful sessions?
[00:03:48] Diego: good question. the runtime supports prefix/KV caching which can dramatically reduce token compute for repeated prefixes. it does require sticky routing for low-latency access to the KV cache. if you have high concurrency, we may need more shards or larger dedicated pools to preserve low p95 latency
[00:04:05] Sana: sticky routing meaning session affinity?
[00:04:08] Diego: yes session affinity by user or conversation id; without it you'll miss cache hits and cost goes up
[00:04:15] Tom: that has implications for autoscaling and burst capacity too, i.e., if we route across nodes we need to ensure hot keys don't bottleneck
[00:04:22] Diego: exact — we'll instrument cache hit rates in the harness and show delta in token compute and latency
[00:04:29] Speaker 1: [crosstalk]
[00:04:31] Maya: other risks? quantization accuracy tradeoffs?
[00:04:34] Diego: quantized models can be 2-3x cheaper but may have small perf deltas on some prompts. we'll run a side-by-side accuracy comparison during the POC
[00:04:43] Rajesh: encryption at rest and in transit?
[00:04:45] Maya: yes, TLS in transit, and customer-managed KMS for keys, plus audit logs. we'll include specifics in the security pack
[00:04:53] Lena: any known multi-region latency constraints? our users are EU/NA so we care about <200ms p95 for short interactions across both regions
[00:05:01] Diego: we can pin region and model variants. dedicated capacity can be region-scoped and we can measure cross-region p95s during the benchmark runs
[00:05:10] Sana: for the traffic model, Diego can you confirm how you'll simulate token variance? we need the harness to reflect that heavy tail of long requests
[00:05:18] Diego: yes i'll shape distributions to match the percentages you gave (70/25/5) and include longer ran sessions for 1% of load to stress KV and memory usage
[00:05:27] Maya: perfect. on success criteria let's list them now so we have alignment: 1) Latency P95 <150ms for short requests on dedicated; 2) cost per 1M tokens within budget threshold (Sana to provide budget number); 3) accuracy regression <=2% on eval set; 4) no functional blockers (SSO, VPC)
[00:05:44] Sana: agreed. budget target — for POC we'll share a target, but long term we want cost at least 30% below our in-house infra numbers
[00:05:53] Tom: and include SLA expectations for Dedicated if we go that route
[00:05:57] Maya: yes we'll put sample SLA in the doc and call out fallback policies and canary rollout options
[00:06:05] Lena: a nit: can the harness emulate websockets and streaming responses? our prod uses streaming a lot
[00:06:12] Diego: yes we have scripts that emulate streaming with partial chunking and measure time-to-first-byte and end-to-end time. that will be part of the harness
[00:06:21] Sana: what about cost modeling — do you provide per-token cost breakdowns including I/O and model compute?
[00:06:27] Maya: we'll provide a cost breakdown and also run a unit economics calc in the POC: tokens/sec, tokens/req, cost per token, and projected monthly cost at X QPS
[00:06:36] Diego: note that caching can change the effective tokens billed significantly; we'll show both cold and warm cache scenarios
[00:06:42] Tom: any compliance docs we should expect?
[00:06:45] Maya: SOC2, ISO if requested, and the security questionnaire. we'll attach them when we send the POC pack
[00:06:50] Rajesh: we'll also need contractual terms for data residency and retention — usually a DPA addendum
[00:06:55] Maya: yep we'll flag legal and have a template DPA and retention options in the enterprise pack
[00:07:01] Speaker 2: [brief pause]
[00:07:03] Lena: ok i'm convinced this is doable. can we recap next steps and who owns what?
[00:07:07] Maya: sure recap — action items: Maya sends POC plan + security docs by Aug 7; Diego builds harness and traffic scripts by Aug 14; Rajesh shares CIDR and KMS requirements by Aug 10; Tom confirms test window and SSO by Aug 12. we'll schedule the run for week of Aug 17.
[00:07:25] Sana: good. one more question — if dedicated capacity is required, what's the lead time to provision?
[00:07:30] Maya: typical lead time for reserved pools is 10-14 days after contract and payment, but for POC we can spin up short-lived dedicated nodes for testing within 48-72 hours in most regions
[00:07:41] Diego: technical caveat: for large memory models and heavy KV cache we may need specific GPU types; we'll call that out in the sizing doc
[00:07:48] Tom: last administrative — please put all artifacts into a shared drive link and share access to our team
[00:07:52] Maya: will do, i'll include the POC doc, benchmark harness link, and a spreadsheet for expected costs
[00:07:58] Speaker 3: [background noise]
[00:08:01] Maya: ok if there's no other questions let's wrap. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack and set up the benchmark run.
[00:08:09] Sana: thanks all
[00:08:10] Tom: thanks
[00:08:12] Lena: thanks
